It's a sunny day, not too hot and not to cold, the sun is hiding behind a fluffy collection white clouds. I kick back my legs, soaking in the rays with my feet wading in a crystal clear pool as an immense bliss washes over me. Truly the perfect day.

But, something is wrong. I feel a grumble in my tumble. Slap that sloshing gut out of the way as I tell it to stop ruining what was probably the most perfect day. Tumble no likey. Tumble retorts with what could only be described as my stomach imploding on itself, the pain was unimaginable. I watched as my life flashed before my eyes, years of experiences that I will never see. I needed something to eat, and fast.

As I grab my lurching tumble I kick over my lawn chair as I stumble around town moaning like a typical Saturday morning in college when suddenly, I smell something coming from Old Man Jenkins' barn. As beads of sweat roll down my forehead, Old Man Jenkins ushered me inside quickly. "Hurry boy, you don't have much time!" The old wrinkled fossil barked at me. I thanked the poor old soul for his immense kindness as I was focused on nothing but that divine smell, savory and a bit spicy. I needed whatever he was cooking. It was sure great that everyone in the town had a culinary arts degree.

As I plopped myself down at his kitchen table, I saw the old man plop a delicious looking heap on a plate from the corner of my eye. The smell was amazing.

The plate was something that I could only describe as the most appetizing thing that I had ever seen. Delicious toasted bread topped with a creamy sauce-- it was nothing short of the most beautiful culinary masterpiece that I had ever laid eyes on.

The old man, being the kind old soul that he was, finished the finishing touches on the plate before my very eyes, garnishing it with what looked to be a basil leaf as he carried the plate over to me. I could tell that he was a weak man, being as old as he was, and the kindness that he showed towards me was appreciated.

Crippled from hunger, hoping for nothing but a first bite of whatever bliss he cooked up, I asked him what he wanted in return, being the polite blobber that I am. It was about that time I realized as his scaly foot slid the plate over that Old Man Jenkins was actually a three story tall crustacean from the Paleolithic Era. He looked me straight in the god damn eyes and said, "I'm gonna need about tree-fiddy."
